title: Measured Fourier transcript with linear-qubit Grover decoding

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the measured Fourier transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under the stated input promise. On every execution branch, total charged work is O(2^(n/2) n^6), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 1. This bound holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the measured Fourier transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under the stated input promise. On every execution branch, peak allocated classical bits is O(n^2), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 0. This bound holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the measured Fourier transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under the stated input promise. On every execution branch, peak allocated qubits is O(n), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 0. This bound holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the measured Fourier transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under the stated input promise. On every execution branch, total samples, exactly 4096n, is O(n), with an absolute constant and envelope growth index exactly 0. This bound holds jointly with the other resource and tolerance claims.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the measured Fourier transcript algorithm in proof.md recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under the stated input promise. The tolerated fraction is epsilon(n)=1/10 among the exactly 4096n acquired samples, with at most floor(4096n/10) corrupt positions. The supplier fixes the corrupted position set before the first acquisition. The reduced joint state on the remaining positions is the tensor product of independent ideal DCP source copies for the same shift. The corrupted registers may contain arbitrary states and be correlated with one another and the supplier. Delivered registers have the specified sizes. All four branchwise resource bounds hold for this configuration.
